1.note: Identification uncertain; transliterated. Possibly a chronicler cited alongside Eusebius, but I cannot confirm who is meant.

2.he: בראשון מדרושיו סי' מ"ז עקר א'
2.note: Apparently Summa Theologiae I, q. 47. The unity of the world is treated there in article 3, not article 1; the author's reference is kept as given.

3.he: ספר תולדות אלכסנדר העשוי מאת חרטומי מצרים
3.note: Probably the Alexander Romance (Pseudo-Callisthenes), whose narrative is framed around Nectanebo, the Egyptian magician-king; the exact text meant is uncertain.

4.note: Sefer Keritot (Samson of Chinon) and Halikhot Olam (Jeshua ha-Levi), both methodological works on Talmudic principles.
